messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated tail latency observed on cont-batch workers in us-west-2. KV cache evictions and paging spikes detected. 35% error budget burn over last 5m. Root TS 3439991234

maria: seeing lots of paging logs: `kvcache: page_in_latency=180ms, eviction_rate=420/s` – service qps is normal but token processing latency is spiking.

devon: any customer reports yet? can we throttle incoming traffic or fallback to smaller model?

sre_kat: customer telemetry shows high p99 for a subset of routes (long-seq generation). A few enterprise tenants noticed 5-10s additional latency, no hard failures yet.

ops_lead: ok triage: looks like continuous-batcher misconfig applied yesterday rolled out a higher `max_batch_tokens` and `max_num_seqs` global default. probable amplification with KV cache hot-pages.

ramon: confirmed — rollout diff: `continuous_batch.default.max_batch_tokens: 8192 -> 16384` and `max_num_seqs: 64 -> 128`. That bumped memory pressure on kvcache and caused page thrash when many long-context requests arrived concurrently.

maria: immediate mitigation idea: revert the config OR apply per-route override for long-seq routes. Reverting global now will be fastest.

devon: +1 revert global and also set `continuation_timeout_ms` lower to force earlier flush from batch. We should aim to reduce `max_batch_tokens` back to 8k and `max_num_seqs` to 64, and set `continuation_timeout_ms: 150` (was 400).

eng_console_bot: deploy-bot: started rollback of contbatch-config v2026.03.14 -> v2026.03.13 (initiated by @maria) — rolling restart of cont-batch-pool nodes (12/24)

onseq logs from worker-17:
```
WARN kvcache paging: page_fault_count=1899, p99_page_read=210ms, mem_pressure=0.78
ERROR contbatch: stalled_kv_lookup seq_id=abcd-1234 duration=2.1s
```

sre_kat: live mitigation checklist while rollback progresses:
- reduce per-route parallelism for known long-seq routes
- enable aggressive eviction policy on kvcache (lru_decay=0.5)
- apply a temporary per-model batch cap (e.g., max_batch_tokens=4096) for T-Model-v2

ops_lead: maria — can you run the per-model patch for T-Model-v2? ramon — can you set eviction policy? I'll coordinate customer comms.

maria: patching now.
```
kubectl patch configmap contbatch-overrides -n redwood --type merge -p '{"data":{"T-Model-v2.max_batch_tokens":"4096","T-Model-v2.max_num_seqs":"32"}}'
```

maria: applied. eng_console_bot confirms change received by routing plane.

ramon: setting eviction policy on kvcache pool (us-west-2 cluster):
```
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/v1/kvcache/pools/us-west-2/eviction -d '{"policy":"lru_decay","decay":0.5}' -H "Authorization: Bearer ${OPS_TOKEN}"
```

ramon: done — response 200. eviction rate target lowered to steady-state.

devon: traffic throttles: can we gate long-seq route to 30rps while we stabilize?

sre_kat: applied rate limit via edge rules for route /generate-long: 120 -> 30 rps for tier:standard. Should reduce bursts.

customer-ps: reached out to two impacted customers with apology + note that we're actively mitigating and will follow up once stable. No escalations yet.

onseq: deploy-bot: rollback progress 12/24 nodes restarted; latency improving on restarted nodes (~40% lower p99).

maria: after 2 minutes of partial rollback, p95 dropped back toward baseline but p99 still elevated on some shards. There are a few noisy tenants causing local hotpages. I've identified tenant ids: tenant_894, tenant_233. Suggest soft-rate limiting those tenants temporarily.

ops_lead: do it and record for follow-up. Customer impact assessment draft: ~3 enterprise customers saw >5s tail; internal error budget at risk but contained. No data loss.

devon: adding an automated check to block global contbatch rollouts if `max_batch_tokens * max_num_seqs` > 1e6 or if kvcache mem_pressure > 0.6 in last 10m. We don't want future single-param changes to multiply unexpectedly.

sre_kat: good. Also adding a canary policy: new batch configs must pass perf-run on canary traffic with synthetic long sequences.

maria: rollback complete 24/24 nodes. cont-batch config reverted. p99 back to baseline for most routes.

ramon: eviction rates normalized. KV cache paging down to nominal: `page_in_latency=22ms, eviction_rate=28/s`

onseq: incident-bot: Incident mitigated — degraded latency resolved. Triage window 12:34 UTC -> 12:52 UTC. Duration ~18m.

ops_lead: summary for follow-up:
- Root cause: unsafe cont-batch global defaults increased batch size and concurrency causing kvcache paging blowup under long-seq workload.
- Immediate mitigations: rollback global config, per-model caps, kvcache eviction tune, per-route rate limits.
- Customer impact: transient p99 tail for ~3 enterprise tenants, no request data loss.
- Action items: (1) add rollout guard for product of batch params (owner @devon, ETA 3d); (2) add canary perf test for batch configs (owner @sre_kat, ETA 1w); (3) add per-tenant throttling quick-path in console (owner @maria, ETA 2w); (4) postmortem writeup (owner @ops_lead, ETA 2d).

maria: taking the postmortem draft. will include logs, diffs, and timeline.

customer-ps: will send follow-up notes to impacted customers once postmortem is ready.

devon: leaving a guardrail in the infra repo now:
```
# contbatch_guard.go snippet
if cfg.MaxBatchTokens*cfg.MaxNumSeqs > 1000000 {
  return fmt.Errorf("unsafe contbatch config: product exceeds threshold")
}
```

sre_kat: handoff to next on-call @ramon at 13:00 UTC. Ramon — we left the rollback in place, per-model overrides set, eviction tuned, throttles applied. Please watch contbatch p99 and kvcache mem_pressure for next 30m.

ramon: ack, monitoring live. will escalate to eng if we see reversion attempts or config churn.

oncall-bot: :white_check_mark: Handoff noted. Next on-call: ramon.

maria: thanks everyone. postmortem action items assigned.

ops_lead: closing thread once postmortem posted. great coordination. :pray:
